items.definition: The word for your mum and your dad together.
items.example: My parents work at the weekend too.

items.definition: The polite word you say before you ask for something. It shows you are asking, not taking.
items.example: Please, can I have the blue cup?

items.definition: A question asking if you are allowed to have something. The person can answer yes or no.
items.example: Can I have a piece of bread?

items.definition: A softer way to ask, good for when you talk to somebody you do not know well.
items.example: Could I have the menu, please?

items.definition: A warm way to say what you want. It is like saying I want, but kinder.
items.example: I would like some orange juice, please.

items.definition: A child who is in the same class as you. Classmates are the easiest people to be friends with.
items.example: Mai is my classmate, and she sits next to me.

items.definition: To say your name to somebody for the first time. It only means saying your name.
items.example: I introduced myself and said, I am An.

items.definition: To start playing with a group that is already playing. You ask first, and then you join in.
items.example: Can I join in your game?

items.definition: To do the same game with another child, side by side. It is the simplest friendship there is.
items.example: We play together at break time every day.

items.definition: A child you have just met. Saying hello twice makes a new child feel welcome.
items.example: I have a new friend in class 4B.

items.definition: The word you say when you meet somebody. You can use it all day long.
items.example: Hello, I am Minh.

items.definition: A short and casual way to say hello, used with people you already know.
items.example: Hi Bao, are you ready?

items.definition: A friendly question you ask after saying hello, to start a small talk.
items.example: Good morning! How are you today?

items.definition: The words you use to tell somebody your own name.
items.example: My name is Lan, and I am seven.

items.definition: What you say the first time you meet somebody. It is polite and warm.
items.example: Nice to meet you. I am Minh.

items.definition: The question word that asks for a thing or an idea. It is the most useful question word of all.
items.example: What does this word mean?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a person.
items.example: Who is your new teacher?

items.definition: Introduces the conditions on a and b.
items.example: ax + b = 0, where a is non-zero.

items.definition: At the time when something happens.
The question word that asks for a reason. Why questions are the most interesting ones.
items.example: Why do we have to sleep?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a way of doing something.
items.example: How do you spell your name?

items.definition: The sun is shining and there are few clouds. A sunny day is a happy day.
items.example: It is sunny, so we can play outside.

items.definition: The sky has clouds in it. Clouds are about the sky, not about the temperature.
items.example: It is cloudy this morning, but it is still warm.

items.definition: Water is falling from the clouds. There is light rain and heavy rain.
items.example: It is rainy, so take an umbrella.

items.definition: The air is moving fast. A windy day can be hot or freezing.
items.example: It is windy, so my hat keeps blowing away.

items.definition: The temperature is low. Cold is lower than cool.
items.example: It is cold outside, so I am wearing my coat.

items.definition: A hot, upset feeling. It often comes fast and shows in your hands and face.
items.example: I feel angry, so I am going to count to ten.

items.definition: A smaller angry feeling that comes when something still will not work.
items.example: I am frustrated with this puzzle.

items.definition: To bring your body back to quiet so you can think and speak.
items.example: Let us calm down first, then talk.

items.definition: To take air in slowly and let it out slowly.
items.example: Breathe in, and blow out slowly.

items.definition: A person you like and who likes you back. Friends like to spend time together.
items.example: Minh is my best friend.

items.definition: Letting somebody use your things, and letting them do things with you too.
items.example: We shared the ball all afternoon.

items.definition: One person goes first, and then the other one goes. It is how two people share one thing fairly.
items.example: We took turns on the swing.

items.definition: Giving your full attention to somebody who is talking.
items.example: He listened to my whole story.

items.definition: When two friends get angry with each other. Every friendship has these.
items.example: We had a quarrel and made up the same afternoon.

items.definition: What you need from somebody else. You can need help with a task, a feeling or a person.
items.example: I need some help with this.

items.definition: To say out loud that you need it. It is not the same as complaining.
items.example: I asked for help and she came straight away.

items.definition: An adult who looks after children, like a parent, a teacher or the school nurse.
items.example: I told a grown-up about it.

items.definition: To make a small attempt before you ask for help.
items.example: I tried first, and then I asked.

items.definition: Polite and friendly towards other people, even when you do not like their food.
items.example: It is kind to say thank you for the food.
